key_insight: A large language model pipeline can extract both cannabis use status and reasons for use from unstructured EHR notes, with fine-tuned GatorTron performing best for use-status classification and an LLM performing best for reasons.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers study symptom-driven cannabis use and treatment outcomes in autoimmune rheumatic disease populations when structured EHR fields are incomplete.
method: Screened 2015–2024 EHR notes with fuzzy keyword matching and 50-word context windows around cannabis mentions.
Annotated 886 snippets for 4-class cannabis use status and 1,027 snippets for 6 reasons-for-use categories.
Compared zero-shot/few-shot prompting and temperature settings with a fine-tuned GatorTron 345M model, then evaluated performance on a held-out validation set.
evidence_signal: The study used expert-labeled snippets and reported model performance on held-out data using accuracy, F1, recall, and precision.
watch_item: Performance may vary across institutions and note styles, so external validation is needed before broad real-world deployment.
paper_title: Extracting patient reported cannabis use and reasons for use from electronic health records: a benchmarking study of large language models
